subject.title: [Bug]: Inbound debounce has no maximum wait — sustained faster-than-debounce input never dispatches and the pending batch grows unbounded

question: Should inbound debounce gain a fixed maximum latency during continuous input, and what shared ceiling or debounceMs ratio should it use?
rationale: Reset-on-message batching was intentional, but its unbounded liveness edge is undesirable; the cross-channel deadline value and contract cannot be selected safely from source behavior alone.

options.title: Bounded shared latency
options.body: Use a documented fixed ceiling or debounceMs ratio and force-flush complete ordered batches without adding configuration.

options.title: Configurable maximum wait
options.body: Expose maxWait as a new setting with aligned schema, metadata, documentation, and upgrade proof.

options.title: Retain quiet-period batching
options.body: Keep pure trailing-edge behavior and explicitly document that continuous input can postpone dispatch indefinitely.

recommendation.title: Bounded shared latency
recommendation.body: Use a documented fixed ceiling or debounceMs ratio and force-flush complete ordered batches without adding configuration.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent ordering work is the strongest current history signal for deciding the shared debouncer contract.
